<!-- generated by docs/generate.sh - edit the javadoc in src/, not this file -->

A variant is a condition written in front of a class, the way tailwind writes them.
`hover:bg-sky-500` is a background that is only there while the cursor is over the element.

Several stack, and every one of them has to hold for the classes behind it to land:

```html
<div class="md:hover:underline"></div>
```

An element's styles are three layers: the plain classes under every layer whose variants are holding,
under whatever was set by hand. Reading the `class` property again replaces everything the classes
said before it.

| Variant | Holds when |
| --- | --- |
| `hover:` | The cursor is over the element or over something inside it, the way css's :hover reaches both. |
| `focus:` | The element has the keyboard. focus-visible is the same thing here: a ctml focus is always shown. |
| `focus-visible:` | The same as focus, there being no ctml focus that is not drawn. |
| `focus-within:` | The element has the keyboard or something inside it does. |
| `active:` | A mouse button is being held on the element or on something inside it. |
| `dark:` | The nearest thing up the tree that says so is drawing dark, or the host says the ui is. |
| `sm:` | The at least 320 gui pixels |
| `md:` | The at least 480 gui pixels |
| `lg:` | The at least 640 gui pixels |
| `xl:` | The at least 854 gui pixels |
| `2xl:` | The at least 1024 gui pixels |
| `max-sm:` | The under 320 gui pixels |
| `max-md:` | The under 480 gui pixels |
| `max-lg:` | The under 640 gui pixels |
| `max-xl:` | The under 854 gui pixels |
| `max-2xl:` | The under 1024 gui pixels |
| `first:` | The element is the first of the ones beside it. |
| `last:` | The element is the last of them. |
| `only:` | The element is the only one there, with nothing beside it. |
| `odd:` | The element is an odd one counting from one, so the first, the third and so on. |
| `even:` | And an even one, so the second, the fourth and so on. |

The breakpoints are gui pixels, not css pixels, since that is what ctml measures in. A minecraft
window at the usual gui scale lands around `md` and `lg` rather than off the end of css's own
numbers.

There are no variants for what ctml cannot answer: no `group-` or `peer-`, since nothing tracks
another element's state for a sibling; no `print`, `motion-reduce` or `contrast-more`, since there is
no such setting to read; and no arbitrary selectors, since there is no selector engine behind them.
Anything else in front of a colon is handed back as an unknown class.
